title_tag: 胡塞一周三袭沙特首都机场，致12死300多人伤！沙特这么有钱、武器这么强，为什么却拿胡塞没办法？—— 美国《纽约时报》外刊讲解第1196天
h1: 胡塞一周三袭沙特首都机场，致12死300多人伤！沙特这么有钱、武器这么强，为什么却拿胡塞没办法？
category: 美国《纽约时报》外刊讲解 第1196天
nav_hint: Saudi Arabia Has Few Options as Houthis Aim at Heart of Its Ambitions

headline.en_html: Saudi Arabia Has Few Options as Houthis Aim at Heart of Its Ambitions — Three deadly attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen on an airport in the Saudi capital underscored the asymmetrical nature of their conflict with the kingdom.
headline.zh: 沙特进退维谷：胡塞武装直指其宏图要害——胡塞武装对沙特首都机场发动的三次致命袭击，凸显了这场冲突的不对称本质。

notes.en: Few options means only a small number of choices are available, suggesting that someone is constrained and has very limited ways to act.
notes.ctx: 标题用它点出沙特的处境：不是无路可走，而是每条路都难走。
notes.ex1: With the deadline approaching, we have few options left. 期限将至，我们几乎已没有选择余地。
notes.ex2: The government has few options but to raise taxes. 政府除了加税几乎没有别的办法。

notes.en: The Houthis are a political and military movement based in northern Yemen, backed by Iran, who seized the capital Sanaa in 2014.
notes.ctx: 标题里的对手方，作者只用这个中性的组织名，不给任何修饰。
notes.ex1: The Houthis control much of northern Yemen, including the capital. 胡塞武装控制着也门北部大部分地区，包括首都。
notes.ex2: Houthi strikes have disrupted shipping in the Red Sea. 胡塞的袭击扰乱了红海航运。

notes.en: To aim at the heart of something means to target its most important or most vulnerable core, rather than its surface.
notes.ctx: 标题说胡塞瞄准的是沙特抱负的要害而非边角，与正文“击中王储宏图核心”前后咬合。
notes.ex1: The scandal struck at the heart of the government's credibility. 这起丑闻直击政府公信力的要害。
notes.ex2: The new policy targets the heart of the housing crisis. 新政策剑指住房危机的核心。

notes.en: Deadly means able to cause death, or causing a great number of deaths.
notes.ctx: 副题用“致命”给三次袭击定性，与后文 12 死、300 余人伤呼应。
notes.ex1: It was the deadliest attack on the city in a decade. 这是该市十年来最致命的一次袭击。
notes.ex2: The storm proved deadly for those caught outdoors. 这场风暴对滞留在户外的人来说是致命的。

notes.en: Iran-backed describes a group or entity that is supported, funded or armed by Iran.
notes.ctx: 副题一上来就给胡塞贴上“伊朗支持”的标签，把冲突框进代理人叙事。
notes.ex1: Iran-backed groups have expanded their influence across the region. 伊朗支持的势力已将影响力扩展到整个地区。
notes.ex2: The U.S.-backed coalition launched a fresh offensive. 美国支持的联军发动了新一轮攻势。

notes.en: To underscore something means to emphasize it or show that it is important.
notes.ctx: 副题说这次袭击“凸显”了冲突本质：把抽象判断落到一个具体事件上。
notes.ex1: The report underscores the urgent need for reform. 这份报告凸显了进行改革的迫切必要性。
notes.ex2: These attacks underscore the fragility of the truce. 这些袭击凸显了停火的脆弱。

notes.en: Asymmetrical means lacking symmetry — in this context, describing a conflict in which the two sides are unequal in strength, tactics and stakes.
notes.ctx: 全文题眼：双方的手段与代价根本不在同一套规则里。
notes.ex1: The rebels rely on asymmetrical tactics such as drones and ambushes. 叛军依靠无人机、伏击等不对称战术。
notes.ex2: Negotiations stalled because of the asymmetrical power balance. 由于力量对比不对称，谈判陷入僵局。

paragraphs.en_html: After the <mark class="voc">deadliest</mark> attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade, <mark class="voc">Crown Prince</mark> Mohammed bin Salman faces growing pressure to find a way to stop the Iran-backed Houthi <mark class="voc">militia</mark> in Yemen from firing missiles and drones at his country. Yet the prince, Saudi Arabia’s <mark class="voc">de facto ruler</mark>, has few options as he confronts an asymmetrical conflict with an <mark class="voc">adversary</mark> that has become stronger since he led a <mark class="voc">disastrous</mark> war against it a decade ago, analysts say.
paragraphs.zh: 十多年来最致命的袭击发生之后，穆罕默德王储面临越来越大的压力，必须设法阻止伊朗支持的也门胡塞武装继续向沙特发射导弹和无人机。然而，这位沙特事实上的统治者几乎没有选择余地——分析人士指出，他面对的是一场不对称冲突，而对手自十年前他发动那场灾难性战争以来，反而变得更加强大。

notes.en: Deadliest is the superlative of deadly, meaning causing the most deaths.
notes.ctx: “十多年来最致命”以时间坐标给事件定级，暗示严重性。
notes.ex1: It was the deadliest earthquake in the region's history. 这是该地区历史上最致命的一次地震。
notes.ex2: This is the deadliest year for journalists on record. 这是有记录以来记者遇害最多的一年。

notes.en: A crown prince is the male heir apparent to a throne.
notes.ctx: 作者用“王储”称呼他，避开“实际国王”的敏感，紧接着又用 de facto ruler 点破真相。
notes.ex1: The crown prince has overseen sweeping economic reforms. 这位王储主导了大规模经济改革。
notes.ex2: The crown prince is seen as the country's de facto leader. 这位王储被视为该国实际上的领导人。

notes.en: A militia is an armed group that is not part of a country's official army, often formed by civilians or a political movement.
notes.ctx: 用“民兵”代指胡塞，暗含非正规、非国家军队的贬抑。
notes.ex1: The militia seized control of the town overnight. 这支民兵一夜之间控制了该城镇。
notes.ex2: Government forces clashed with militias in the north. 政府军在北部与民兵发生冲突。

notes.en: A de facto ruler is someone who holds real power, even if they do not hold the official title.
notes.ctx: 国王是老萨勒曼，真正掌权的是王储——一个词说破沙特权力结构。
notes.ex1: He is the de facto leader of the party. 他是该党实际上的领导人。
notes.ex2: English is the de facto language of business here. 英语是此地事实上的商务语言。

notes.en: An adversary is an opponent or enemy in a conflict or competition.
notes.ctx: 不用 enemy 而用“对手”，语气中性，把战争写成力量对比而非正义讨伐。
notes.ex1: She defeated a formidable adversary in the final. 她在决赛中战胜了一位强劲的对手。
notes.ex2: The two countries have been adversaries for decades. 这两个国家几十年来一直是对手。

notes.en: Disastrous means extremely bad or causing great harm and failure.
notes.ctx: 给十年前的也门战争定性：不但没赢，还帮对手练了级。
notes.ex1: The decision proved disastrous for the whole region. 这一决定对整个地区而言被证明是灾难性的。
notes.ex2: Poor planning led to a disastrous outcome. 糟糕的规划导致了灾难性的结果。

paragraphs.en_html: The Houthis have <mark class="voc">carried out</mark> three fatal attacks on an international airport in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, over the past week. Those included a strike on a passenger terminal on Saturday that killed at least 12 people and injured more than 300, many of them <mark class="voc">critically</mark>, according to the Saudi authorities. They have also hit at the heart of Prince Mohammed’s ambitions to <mark class="voc">transform</mark> Saudi Arabia from an <mark class="voc">insular</mark>, <mark class="voc">oil-dependent</mark> nation into a global <mark class="voc">hub</mark> for business and tourism.
paragraphs.zh: 过去一周，胡塞武装对沙特首都利雅得的一座国际机场发动了三次致命袭击，其中周六针对航站楼的袭击造成至少12人死亡、300多人受伤，许多人伤势危重——数字来自沙特当局。这些袭击也击中了穆罕默德王储宏图的核心：他要把沙特从一个封闭、依赖石油的国家，变成全球商业和旅游的枢纽。

notes.en: To carry out something means to perform or complete a task or action.
notes.ctx: 用“实施”而非 attack，暗示三次袭击是有预谋、有组织的行动。
notes.ex1: The group carried out a series of coordinated attacks. 该组织实施了一系列协同袭击。
notes.ex2: The team carried out tests over six months. 团队在六个月内开展了测试。

notes.en: Critically, in a medical context, means in a very serious or life-threatening condition.
notes.ctx: 五个词很轻，信息很重：伤者危重，意味着死亡数字还可能上升。
notes.ex1: Ten passengers remain critically injured. 已有十名乘客仍伤势危重。
notes.ex2: She was critically ill but has since recovered. 她一度病危，但后来康复了。

notes.en: To transform something into something else means to change it completely, often improving it.
notes.ctx: 一句话说完“2030 愿景”的野心：从石油国家转向商业与旅游枢纽。
notes.ex1: The city has transformed itself into a financial hub. 这座城市已将自己转型为金融中心。
notes.ex2: Technology has transformed the way we work. 科技已彻底改变了我们的工作方式。

notes.en: Insular means narrow-minded or isolated, uninterested in outside ideas.
notes.ctx: 给改革前的沙特画像：只靠石油、不与外界来往。
notes.ex1: The village remained insular for generations. 这个村子几代人都与外界隔绝。
notes.ex2: Critics say the industry is too insular. 批评者称这个行业过于封闭。

notes.en: Oil-dependent describes an economy that relies heavily on oil revenues.
notes.ctx: 与 insular 并列，精准概括旧经济结构，也暗示转型的紧迫。
notes.ex1: The oil-dependent economy is vulnerable to price swings. 依赖石油的经济对价格波动十分脆弱。
notes.ex2: The government wants to move away from an oil-dependent model. 政府希望摆脱依赖石油的模式。

notes.en: A hub is the central or most important point of an activity, network or region.
notes.ctx: 用“枢纽”而非 center，强调汇聚与辐射的功能。
notes.ex1: Dubai has become a global hub for trade. 迪拜已成为全球贸易枢纽。
notes.ex2: The airport is a major hub for connecting flights. 该机场是重要的中转枢纽。

paragraphs.en_html: But there is <mark class="voc">no easy way</mark> for the crown prince to <mark class="voc">halt</mark> the Houthis’ attacks. A political resolution with the militia has become increasingly difficult to reach as its confidence and demands grow, and attempting to <mark class="voc">defeat</mark> the Houthis <mark class="voc">militarily</mark> is unlikely to work either, analysts say. The group has <mark class="voc">little to lose</mark>, and has become increasingly <mark class="voc">battle-hardened</mark> after repeated confrontations with powerful, wealthier enemies.
paragraphs.zh: 但王储想叫停胡塞的袭击，并没有轻松的办法。随着这支武装的信心与诉求水涨船高，与之达成政治解决愈发困难；而试图在军事上击败它，同样不太可能奏效——分析人士如是说。这个组织没什么可失去的，又在与更强大、更富有的对手的一次次交手中，被磨炼得越发身经百战。

notes.en: No easy way means there is no simple or painless solution.
notes.ctx: 不是没有办法，而是办法都不轻松——全文“死局”的第一次明说。
notes.ex1: There is no easy way to solve this problem. 这个问题没有轻松的解法。
notes.ex2: Taking the shortcut offers no easy way forward. 走捷径并不是轻松的前行之路。

notes.en: To halt something means to stop it, especially something that is already moving or ongoing.
notes.ctx: 比 stop 更正式，暗示这本该是要调动国家力量才能完成的动作。
notes.ex1: The government halted all new construction. 政府叫停了所有新开工项目。
notes.ex2: The train came to a halt at the station. 火车在车站停了下来。

notes.en: To defeat someone means to win against them in a battle, war or contest.
notes.ctx: 提出“军事上击败”这条方案，随即被 unlikely to work 否定。
notes.ex1: They tried to defeat the rebels by force. 他们试图以武力击败叛军。
notes.ex2: The bill was defeated in parliament. 该法案在议会遭否决。

notes.en: Militarily means by means of armed force or in military terms.
notes.ctx: 把军事手段单独拎出来评判，与政治途径形成双线对比。
notes.ex1: The conflict cannot be solved militarily. 这场冲突无法靠军事手段解决。
notes.ex2: The country is militarily stronger but politically isolated. 该国军事上更强，政治上却更孤立。

notes.en: To have little to lose means to be in a position where you have almost nothing left that can be damaged, so you are not afraid of further risk.
notes.ctx: 全文钥匙句：胡塞控制区已被打烂，所以任何威胁都失效。
notes.ex1: With nothing to lose, they decided to fight on. 他们已经无所顾忌，决定继续战斗。
notes.ex2: He felt he had little to lose by speaking out. 他觉得直言不讳也没什么可失去的。

notes.en: Battle-hardened describes troops who have become tough and skilful through repeated combat.
notes.ctx: 沙特每升级一次打击，反而给对手加了一层经验值。
notes.ex1: The battle-hardened unit was sent to the front line. 这支久经沙场的部队被派往前线。
notes.ex2: Years of conflict had hardened the fighters. 多年冲突把这些战士磨砺得更加坚韧。

paragraphs.en_html: “The only <mark class="voc">realistic</mark> solution for the Saudis is <mark class="voc">an end to</mark> the Iranian-American war, in which the U.S. <mark class="voc">gets</mark> the Iranians to <mark class="voc">commit the Houthis to</mark> <mark class="voc">an end of hostilities</mark> as part of the overall deal,” said F. Gregory Gause, a Saudi specialist at the Middle East Institute. “Unfortunately for the Saudis, it is not clear how much President Trump <mark class="voc">listens</mark> to them on this.”
paragraphs.zh: 中东研究所的沙特问题专家F. 格雷戈里·高斯说：“对沙特而言，唯一现实的出路，是结束伊朗和美国之间的这场战争——由美国出面，让伊朗约束胡塞，使其承诺停止敌对行动，作为整体协议的一部分。”他接着说：“对沙特不利的是，在这件事上，特朗普总统究竟听他们几分，并不明朗。”

notes.en: Realistic means achievable and sensible given the actual situation.
notes.ctx: “唯一现实”等于说其他方案不是不可能，而是根本行不通。
notes.ex1: We need a realistic plan, not a wish list. 我们需要一份现实的方案，而不是一厢情愿的清单。
notes.ex2: It is not realistic to expect instant results. 指望立竿见影是不现实的。

notes.en: An end to something means the termination or stopping of it.
notes.ctx: 专家把胡塞问题的钥匙，直接放到了华盛顿与德黑兰之间。
notes.ex1: Everyone hopes for an end to the fighting. 人人都希望战事结束。
notes.ex2: The deal brought an end to years of dispute. 这份协议结束了多年的争端。

notes.en: To get someone to do something means to persuade or arrange for them to do it.
notes.ctx: “美国让伊朗去约束胡塞”——一个“我着你，你看他”的三级传导结构。
notes.ex1: She got him to fix the leak. 她让他去修好了漏水。
notes.ex2: Can you get the team to deliver on time? 你能让团队按时交付吗？

notes.en: To commit someone to something means to make them formally promise or obligate themselves to it.
notes.zh: 使某人承诺（受约束于）某事
notes.ctx: 用承诺把对方捆住，比单纯“要求”更有约束力。
notes.ex1: The company committed itself to cutting emissions by half. 该公司承诺将排放量减半。
notes.ex2: He refused to commit to a date. 他拒绝承诺具体日期。

notes.en: An end of hostilities means the cessation of armed conflict.
notes.ctx: 用“结束敌对”而非“停火”，要的不是喘口气，而是彻底了结。
notes.ex1: Both sides agreed to a cessation of hostilities. 双方同意停止敌对行动。
notes.ex2: Hostilities resumed after the truce collapsed. 停火破裂后，敌对行动重新开始。

notes.en: To listen to someone on something means to take their views seriously regarding that matter.
notes.zh: 在某事上听取某人意见
notes.ctx: 一个平常词组，写出盟友之间的“分量焦虑”：沙特说的话还有几分重量。
notes.ex1: The president rarely listens to his advisers on trade. 总统在贸易问题上很少听取顾问的意见。
notes.ex2: She felt she was not being listened to. 她觉得没人听她的。

paragraphs.en_html: In two weeks, Prince Mohammed is planning to host his <mark class="voc">flagship</mark> annual investment summit, during which world leaders, billionaires and executives were expected to <mark class="voc">descend upon</mark> the city to <mark class="voc">hobnob with</mark> Saudi officials and fund managers. “The problem for the Saudis is that they experience more damage from Houthi strikes on their infrastructure <mark class="voc">than the other way around</mark>,” Mr. Gause said. “A strike on Riyadh Airport could lead someone thinking about investing in the country to reconsider.”
paragraphs.zh: 两周后，穆罕默德王储本将主办他的旗舰年度投资峰会，届时各国政要、亿万富翁和企业高管预计会涌入这座城市，与沙特官员和基金经理推杯换盏。高斯说：“沙特的问题是，胡塞打击其基础设施给它造成的损失，要比反过来大得多。一次对利雅得机场的袭击，就可能让那些正在考虑投资这个国家的人重新掂量。”

notes.en: Flagship describes the most important or representative thing of its kind.
notes.ctx: 强调这不是普通会议，而是王储压箱底的门面。
notes.ex1: The new phone is the company's flagship product. 这款新手机是公司的旗舰产品。
notes.ex2: Their flagship store opened in the city center. 他们的旗舰店在市中心开业。

notes.en: To descend upon a place means to arrive in large numbers and with a sense of occasion.
notes.ctx: 把政要富豪写成“浩浩荡荡杀过来”，语气略带调侃。
notes.ex1: Reporters descended upon the small town. 记者们蜂拥而至这座小镇。
notes.ex2: Tourists descend on the island every summer. 每年夏天游客涌入这座岛。

notes.en: To hobnob with someone means to socialize with wealthy or powerful people in a familiar, informal way.
notes.ctx: 全篇最松弛、最“损”的一处：不是共商大计，而是扎堆 social。
notes.ex1: He spent the evening hobnobbing with investors. 他整晚都在和投资人套近乎。
notes.ex2: She dislikes hobnobbing with the rich. 她不喜欢和有钱人应酬。

notes.en: Than the other way around means 'than the reverse' — comparing one direction of an exchange with its opposite.
notes.ctx: 一句话点出真正的不对称：沙特有值钱的东西可打，胡塞没有。
notes.ex1: I thought you worked for her, not the other way around. 我以为你为她工作，而不是反过来。
notes.ex2: It is the students who teach the teacher, not the other way around. 是学生在教老师，而不是反过来。

paragraphs.en_html: In recent days, the Houthi military spokesman, Yahya Saree, has <mark class="voc">issued</mark> repeated <mark class="voc">warnings</mark> to airlines and travelers against using Saudi airports, declaring them a “<mark class="voc">theater of operations</mark> for our forces.”
paragraphs.zh: 近几天，胡塞军方发言人叶海亚·萨雷一再向航空公司和旅客发出警告，劝阻他们使用沙特机场，并宣布这些机场是“我方部队的作战区域”。

notes.en: To issue something means to formally release or give it out, such as a statement or warning.
notes.ctx: 用“发布”而非 give，暗示这是官方声明，不是随口一说。
notes.ex1: The agency issued a travel warning. 该机构发布了旅行警告。
notes.ex2: They issued a statement denying the claims. 他们发表声明否认这些说法。

notes.en: A warning is a statement telling someone about possible danger or a problem.
notes.ctx: 这不是抗议，而是提前通告：机场已被划进打击清单。
notes.ex1: The company ignored the safety warnings. 公司无视了安全警告。
notes.ex2: The attack came without warning. 袭击毫无预警地发生了。

notes.en: A theater of operations is a military term for the geographic area in which military operations are conducted.
notes.ctx: 用军事术语定义民用机场，潜台词是“这里已是战场，你敢来后果自负”。
notes.ex1: Troops were deployed to the theater of operations. 部队被部署到战区。
notes.ex2: The general took command of the entire theater. 这位将军接管了整个战区。

paragraphs.en_html: The Houthis, who <mark class="voc">rule over</mark> <mark class="voc">bomb-scarred</mark> countryside where most critical infrastructure has already been destroyed, appear to be <mark class="voc">calculating</mark> that they can <mark class="voc">inflict more pain on</mark> Saudi Arabia, one of the world’s largest exporters of oil, than the kingdom can inflict on them, analysts say.
paragraphs.zh: 胡塞统治着一片饱受轰炸摧残的乡村地带，那里大部分关键基础设施早已被摧毁。分析人士说，他们似乎正在盘算：自己能给沙特——世界最大的石油出口国之一——造成的痛苦，要多于沙特能给他们造成的痛苦。

notes.en: To rule over a place means to govern or control it, often with strong authority.
notes.ctx: 用“统治”而非 govern，暗示那是军事控制，不是治理。
notes.ex1: The group has ruled over the region for years. 该组织已统治该地区多年。
notes.ex2: He ruled the empire with an iron fist. 他以铁腕统治这个帝国。

notes.en: Bomb-scarred describes a place marked and damaged by years of bombing.
notes.ctx: 一个词自带画面：土地像被划满伤疤，说明战争已持续很久。
notes.ex1: The bomb-scarred city slowly began to rebuild. 这座饱受轰炸的城市开始缓慢重建。
notes.ex2: Children played among the war-scarred buildings. 孩子们在布满战痕的建筑间玩耍。

notes.en: Calculating describes someone who carefully plans and weighs outcomes, often in a cold, self-interested way.
notes.ctx: 说明胡塞不是冲动报复，而是在冷静地算一道成本收益题。
notes.ex1: She gave him a calculating look. 她用算计的眼神看了他一眼。
notes.ex2: He is a calculating and patient negotiator. 他是个精于算计、极有耐心的谈判者。

notes.en: To inflict pain on someone means to cause them to suffer pain or damage.
notes.ctx: 点出胡塞的战略逻辑：比的不是谁赢，而是谁更能让对方疼。
notes.ex1: The sanctions inflicted severe damage on the economy. 制裁对经济造成了严重破坏。
notes.ex2: They inflicted heavy losses on the enemy. 他们给敌人造成了重大损失。

paragraphs.en_html: The <mark class="voc">escalation</mark> of violence between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis began in July, when an <mark class="voc">airstrike</mark> hit the international airport in Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, which the Houthis control. The Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out the attack. The Saudi-backed Yemeni government <mark class="voc">claimed responsibility for</mark> the strike, and said it had been acting to prevent an <mark class="voc">unauthorized</mark> Iranian plane from landing. The attack on Sanaa airport <mark class="voc">set off</mark> <mark class="voc">a chain of events</mark> that <mark class="voc">culminated</mark> last week in a return to <mark class="voc">full-blown</mark> war between the Houthis, and Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government.
paragraphs.zh: 沙特与胡塞之间的暴力升级始于7月：当时一次空袭击中了也门首都萨那的国际机场，而萨那由胡塞控制。胡塞指责沙特是幕后推手；沙特支持的也门政府则宣称对这次袭击负责，称其当时是为了阻止一架未经授权的伊朗飞机降落。对萨那机场的袭击引发了一连串事件，最终在上周演变成胡塞与沙特及也门政府之间全面战争的重燃。

notes.en: Escalation means a gradual increase in intensity or severity, especially of conflict.
notes.ctx: 局势像扶梯一样一格一格往上走，最终回到全面战争。
notes.ex1: Both sides called for de-escalation. 双方都呼吁局势降温。
notes.ex2: The escalation of the conflict alarmed the region. 冲突升级令整个地区警觉。

notes.en: An airstrike is an attack carried out by aircraft.
notes.ctx: 用“空袭”而非 bombing，更职业、更短促。
notes.ex1: The military launched airstrikes on the base. 军方对该基地发动了空袭。
notes.ex2: Airstrikes hit the city overnight. 空袭在夜间袭击了这座城市。

notes.en: To claim responsibility for something means to state publicly that one carried it out.
notes.ctx: “认领”袭击的竟然是一个政府；作者用 claimed 保留距离，不为其背书。
notes.ex1: No group has claimed responsibility for the attack. 尚无组织宣称对此次袭击负责。
notes.ex2: The militants claimed responsibility in a video. 武装分子在视频中宣称对此负责。

notes.en: Unauthorized means not officially approved or permitted.
notes.ctx: 也门政府给行动找的理由，等于把矛头指向伊朗——但作者只做转述。
notes.ex1: Unauthorized access to the system is prohibited. 禁止未经授权访问该系统。
notes.ex2: The report was based on an unauthorized leak. 这份报告基于未经授权的泄露。

notes.en: To set off something means to cause it to start, especially a chain of events or an explosion.
notes.ctx: 像点燃引信：一个事件引爆一连串事件。
notes.ex1: The incident set off a wave of protests. 这起事件引发了一波抗议。
notes.ex2: His remarks set off a heated debate. 他的言论引发了激烈争论。

notes.en: A chain of events is a series of connected incidents where each leads to the next.
notes.ctx: 把七月到上周的整条时间线，一句话串起来。
notes.ex1: A single decision triggered a chain of events. 一个决定引发了一连串事件。
notes.ex2: The accident was the start of a chain of events. 这场事故是一连串事件的开端。

notes.en: To culminate in something means to reach a final result after a gradual process.
notes.ctx: 强调一路升级到顶点才爆发，不是简单“结束”。
notes.ex1: Years of tension culminated in war. 多年紧张局势最终演变为战争。
notes.ex2: The festival culminates in a fireworks display. 节日以烟花表演收尾。

notes.en: Full-blown means fully developed or complete, at the highest stage.
notes.ctx: 与 conflict、skirmish 构成烈度阶梯：从局部摩擦到全面战争。
notes.ex1: The dispute has become a full-blown crisis. 这场争端已演变成全面危机。
notes.ex2: What began as a rumor became a full-blown scandal. 一个传言最终演变成全面丑闻。

paragraphs.en_html: The Houthis <mark class="voc">rose to power</mark> in 2014, when the militia <mark class="voc">took over</mark> Sanaa, <mark class="voc">routing</mark> the internationally recognized government. Soon after, Prince Mohammed, in one of his first acts as Saudi Arabia’s 29-year-old minister of defense, <mark class="voc">pledged</mark> to restore the Yemeni government by declaring war against the Houthis, at the time a <mark class="voc">ragtag</mark> group of <mark class="voc">rebels</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 胡塞武装在2014年崛起掌权：这一年，他们攻占萨那，击溃了国际社会承认的政府。不久后，当时年仅29岁的穆罕默德王储，在担任沙特国防大臣后的最初举措之一中，宣布向胡塞开战，誓言恢复也门政府——而在当时，胡塞不过是一群乌合之众。

notes.en: To rise to power means to come into a position of authority or control.
notes.ctx: 把一次武装夺权写成“顺势而起”，语气克制。
notes.ex1: He rose to power after years of struggle. 经过多年奋斗，他登上了权力之巅。
notes.ex2: The party came to power in 2010. 该党于2010年上台执政。

notes.en: To take over something means to assume control of it.
notes.ctx: 与 rule over 呼应，都强调以力量控制。
notes.ex1: The rebels took over the capital in days. 叛军数日内便攻占了首都。
notes.ex2: She took over the project last month. 她上个月接手了这个项目。

notes.en: To rout someone means to defeat them completely and drive them away in disorder.
notes.ctx: 不是“赢了”，是“打崩了、打散了”。
notes.ex1: The army was routed in a single battle. 这支军队在一场战役中被打得溃不成军。
notes.ex2: They routed their opponents in the final. 他们在决赛中横扫对手。

notes.en: To pledge to do something means to make a formal and serious promise to do it.
notes.ctx: 把这次表态写成庄严的国家承诺——正因如此，后面被打脸才格外讽刺。
notes.ex1: The government pledged to cut poverty by half. 政府承诺将贫困削减一半。
notes.ex2: Donors pledged billions in aid. 捐助方承诺提供数十亿援助。

notes.en: Ragtag describes a group that is disorganized, scruffy and lacking proper equipment.
notes.ctx: 十年前的胡塞与今天“久经沙场、自给自足”的形象形成最强反差。
notes.ex1: They were a ragtag group of volunteers with almost no training. 他们是一群几乎没有受过训练的杂牌志愿者。
notes.ex2: The ragtag militia grew into a formidable force. 这支乌合之众逐渐壮大成一支劲旅。

notes.en: A rebel is a person who fights against a government or authority.
notes.ctx: 与 ragtag 连用，“叛军”二字带出作者立场。
notes.ex1: Rebel fighters advanced toward the city. 叛军向该城推进。
notes.ex2: The rebels refused to surrender. 叛军拒绝投降。

paragraphs.en_html: The prince, now 41, has <mark class="voc">consolidated</mark> his power <mark class="voc">inside Saudi Arabia and beyond</mark>. Yet the Yemeni militia has also become stronger and more <mark class="voc">self-sufficient</mark>, and it <mark class="voc">poses</mark> a more <mark class="voc">intractable</mark> challenge than <mark class="voc">any other</mark> he has faced.
paragraphs.zh: 如今41岁的王储，已在沙特国内外巩固了自己的权力。然而，也门的这支武装同样变得更强、更能自给自足，它给王储出的难题，是他迄今面对过的最棘手的一道。

notes.en: To consolidate power means to strengthen and make power more secure.
notes.ctx: 把王储从“新人”到“实权者”的蜕变一句话说完。
notes.ex1: The president moved to consolidate his grip on power. 总统着手巩固其对权力的掌控。
notes.ex2: The team consolidated its lead in the second half. 球队在下半场巩固了领先优势。

notes.en: Inside something and beyond means within it and also further out, implying influence extends widely.
notes.ctx: 三个词写完他的国际影响力：不止国境之内。
notes.ex1: Her influence extends within the party and beyond. 她的影响力遍及党内乃至更广范围。
notes.ex2: The brand is known at home and abroad. 这个品牌在国内外都很有名。

notes.en: Self-sufficient means able to provide for oneself without outside help.
notes.ctx: 全文最关键的隐藏信息：胡塞不再完全依赖伊朗，“掐援助”这张牌越来越不好用。
notes.ex1: The village is almost self-sufficient in food. 这个村子在粮食上几乎自给自足。
notes.ex2: The company aims to become self-sufficient in energy. 该公司力求在能源上实现自给自足。

notes.en: To pose a challenge means to present a difficulty or test.
notes.ctx: 用 pose 而非 is，把挑战写成悬在面前的难题。
notes.ex1: Climate change poses a serious challenge to farmers. 气候变化给农民带来了严峻挑战。
notes.ex2: The new rules pose difficulties for small firms. 新规给小企业带来困难。

notes.en: Intractable describes a problem that is very difficult to control or solve.
notes.ctx: difficult 只是“难”，intractable 是“难到无从下手”，中文最贴切的是“死结”。
notes.ex1: Poverty remains an intractable problem in the region. 贫困在该地区仍是一个难解的问题。
notes.ex2: The two sides are locked in an intractable dispute. 双方陷入了一场难以化解的争端。

notes.en: Any other means any single one besides the one already mentioned.
notes.ctx: 把十二年任内所有难题都拉进对比，凸显这个挑战之最。
notes.ex1: This challenge is tougher than any other he has faced. 这个挑战比他所面对的任何其他挑战都更难。
notes.ex2: She knows the city better than any other visitor. 她比任何其他游客都更了解这座城市。

paragraphs.en_html: After the strike on Sanaa airport, the Houthis, who have long <mark class="voc">bristled at</mark> restrictions on their <mark class="voc">airspace</mark> that are <mark class="voc">enforced</mark> by Saudi Arabia, announced that they intended to enforce a “<mark class="voc">blockade</mark> for blockade” policy. They <mark class="voc">declared an embargo on</mark> Saudi shipping in the Red Sea, which has become an important alternative route for Saudi oil exports after the Iran war disrupted <mark class="voc">shipments</mark> through the Strait of Hormuz.
paragraphs.zh: 萨那机场遇袭后，长期以来对沙特强制实施的领空限制耿耿于怀的胡塞宣布，将奉行“以封锁对封锁”的政策，对红海上的沙特航运实施禁运。由于伊朗战争打乱了经霍尔木兹海峡的货运，红海早已成为沙特石油出口的一条重要替代通道——如今，这条通道也被盯上了。

notes.en: To bristle at something means to react with anger or resentment.
notes.ctx: 写出胡塞积压已久的怒气，为“以封锁对封锁”的报复铺垫。
notes.ex1: She bristled at the suggestion that she was wrong. 听到暗示她错了，她顿时火冒三丈。
notes.ex2: He bristled with indignation at the insult. 面对这番侮辱，他怒不可遏。

notes.en: Airspace is the portion of the sky above a country that it controls.
notes.ctx: 封锁领空是主权行为，胡塞被锁多年，如今反手锁沙特的海路。
notes.ex1: The country closed its airspace to foreign flights. 该国对外国航班关闭了领空。
notes.ex2: The plane entered restricted airspace. 这架飞机进入了受限空域。

notes.en: To enforce something means to make people obey a rule or law.
notes.ctx: 同一个词两面用：沙特“强制”限制，胡塞也要“强制”封锁。
notes.ex1: Police are enforcing the new speed limits. 警方正在执行新的限速规定。
notes.ex2: The rules are difficult to enforce. 这些规定难以强制执行。

notes.en: A blockade is an act of surrounding a place to prevent goods or people from entering or leaving.
notes.ctx: 准战争行为，比 embargo 更全面、更强硬；引号说明这是胡塞自己的说法。
notes.ex1: The navy imposed a blockade on the port. 海军对该港口实施了封锁。
notes.ex2: Aid ships were blocked by the blockade. 救援船只被封锁拦下。

notes.en: To declare an embargo on something means to officially ban trade or shipping with a target.
notes.ctx: 把战场从陆地、空中延伸到海上的一步。
notes.ex1: The UN imposed an arms embargo on the country. 联合国对该国实施了武器禁运。
notes.ex2: The oil embargo sent prices soaring. 石油禁运令油价飙升。

notes.en: A shipment is a quantity of goods sent from one place to another.
notes.ctx: 被打乱的是石油运输——沙特的经济命脉。
notes.ex1: Oil shipments were halted for days. 石油运输中断了数日。
notes.ex2: The shipment arrived two weeks late. 这批货晚到了两周。

paragraphs.en_html: Prince Turki Al Faisal, a senior Saudi royal and a former Saudi intelligence chief, said that while the kingdom had always preferred “<mark class="voc">restraint</mark>” in its foreign policy, the Houthis had <mark class="voc">exceeded</mark> the limits of the Saudi leadership’s patience. “Restraint is <mark class="voc">no longer</mark> <mark class="voc">operable</mark>,” he said in an interview last week with a Saudi newspaper, Arab News.
paragraphs.zh: 沙特高级王室成员、前沙特情报机构负责人图尔基·费萨尔亲王表示，尽管沙特在外交政策上历来偏好“克制”，但胡塞已经超出了沙特领导层耐心的极限。他上周在接受沙特《阿拉伯新闻》采访时说：“克制，已不再可行。”

notes.en: Restraint is the quality of controlling oneself and not acting on impulse, especially when one could retaliate.
notes.ctx: 引号暗示这只是外界（也是沙特自己）贴的标签，全文结尾要撕掉的正是它。
notes.ex1: Both sides urged restraint. 双方都呼吁保持克制。
notes.ex2: He showed remarkable restraint under pressure. 他在压力下表现出非凡的克制。

notes.en: To exceed something means to go beyond a limit or expectation.
notes.ctx: “超出耐心的极限”，比“很生气”高级太多。
notes.ex1: Demand far exceeded supply. 需求远超供给。
notes.ex2: The cost exceeded our budget. 成本超出了我们的预算。

notes.en: No longer means not any more; something that was once true is not true now.
notes.ctx: 藏着“曾经可行、如今不行”的时间断裂，正是这句金句的杀伤力所在。
notes.ex1: The old rules are no longer operable. 旧规则已不再可行。
notes.ex2: He is no longer with the company. 他已不在该公司任职。

notes.en: Operable means able to be put into practice or made to work.
notes.ctx: 全文最佳金句：把“克制”从态度问题改写成可不可行的问题。
notes.ex1: The old safety rules are no longer operable. 旧的安全规程已不再可行。
notes.ex2: The plan is only operable with more funding. 这项计划只有在增加资金后才可行。

proper.name: Houthis / 胡塞武装
proper.def:
也门的政治军事组织，2014年夺取首都萨那并控制也门北部；与沙特领导的联军长期交战，被多方视为伊朗支持的代理人武装。
本文中的意思：全文“对手方”。作者用Houthis / militia / group 交替称呼，态度冷峻克制，不附加任何形容词。

proper.name: Mohammed bin Salman / 穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼
proper.def:
沙特王储、实际统治者，外界简称MBS。2016年推出“2030愿景”，29岁时以国防部长身份主导也门战争。
本文中的意思：全文“主角”。文章写他29岁宣战、41岁面对困局，用年龄跨度暗示十年来的战略失败。

proper.name: Vision 2030 / 2030愿景
proper.def:
沙特2016年推出的国家经济转型计划，核心目标是摆脱石油依赖，发展旅游、娱乐、科技与私营经济；NEOM、红海旅游项目、未来投资倡议大会均是其招牌。
本文中的意思：标题中ambitions的具体所指。机场被炸直接威胁沙特向世界展示“开放、安全、值得投资”的形象。

proper.name: Iranian-American war / 美伊战争
proper.def:
文中指美国与伊朗之间的战争状态；霍尔木兹海峡航运因此受阻，沙特石油出口被迫改走红海。
本文中的意思：专家指出“结束美伊战争”才是沙特唯一的现实出路——暗示沙特自己的命运钥匙握在华盛顿和德黑兰手里。

proper.name: F. Gregory Gause / F. 格雷戈里·高斯（中东研究所）
proper.def:
高斯是美国研究沙特与海湾政治的资深学者；中东研究所是华盛顿老牌智库，以中东问题分析著称。
本文中的意思：文章的主要引语来源。他的判断为“沙特选项有限”“投资人会望而却步”等观点提供权威背书。

proper.name: Future Investment Initiative (FII) / 未来投资倡议大会（沙漠达沃斯）
proper.def:
沙特一年一度的旗舰投资峰会，2017年首次在利雅得举办，被称为“沙漠达沃斯”；2018年曾因卡舒吉事件遭多家西方企业抵制。
本文中的意思：王储推销沙特转型的头号平台。机场被炸恰逢峰会前夕，直接威胁参会者与投资信心。

proper.name: Yahya Saree / 叶海亚·萨雷
proper.def:
胡塞武装的军事发言人，常通过媒体发布袭击声明与威胁。
本文中的意思：他的警告“沙特机场是我军作战区域”被作者引用，坐实胡塞把民用机场军事化的强硬姿态。

proper.name: Sanaa / 萨那
proper.def:
也门首都，2014年被胡塞武装夺取后成为其政治中心。
本文中的意思：冲突时间线的起点——7月萨那机场遇袭，触发后续连锁反应，让战争回到全面升级状态。

proper.name: the Strait of Hormuz / 霍尔木兹海峡
proper.def:
波斯湾通往印度洋的唯一出口，全球约五分之一石油贸易经此运输，被称为“世界油阀”。
本文中的意思：美伊战争让这条主航道受阻，沙特才被迫改走红海；红海再被封锁，等于两条油路全断。

proper.name: the Red Sea / 红海
proper.def:
非洲与阿拉伯半岛之间的海域，经苏伊士运河连接地中海，是全球航运与能源贸易的重要通道。
本文中的意思：霍尔木兹受阻后，红海成为沙特石油出口的替代路线；胡塞对红海航运的封锁使沙特经济命脉进一步承压。

proper.name: Prince Turki Al Faisal / 图尔基·费萨尔亲王
proper.def:
沙特资深王室成员、前情报总局局长（1979–2001），曾任驻美大使，是王室中少数敢于公开发声的人物。
本文中的意思：文章把“克制已不再可行”这句最重的话交给他——体制内的人发信号，暗示沙特官方立场可能发生历史性转变。

proper.name: Arab News / 《阿拉伯新闻》
proper.def:
沙特主要的英文日报，官方色彩浓厚，面向海湾地区外籍人士与英语读者。
本文中的意思：作者特意交代这句强硬表态出自《阿拉伯新闻》上周采访，强化“这是官方放风、不是个人意见”的可信度。

practice.intro: 请将以下中文句子翻译为英文。要求：尽量用上本文的核心表达，可以适当改变词形，但不要直接照抄原文。
items: 然而，作为沙特实际上的统治者，这位王储几乎没有多少选择，因为他面对着一场与一个敌手的不对称冲突——而这个敌手，自从十年前他对其发动那场灾难性的战争以来，反而变得更强了。分析人士如是说。
这些袭击还击中了穆罕默德王储抱负的核心：他要把沙特从一个封闭的、依赖石油的国家，转型为全球商业和旅游中心。
胡塞武装统治着饱受轰炸创伤的乡村地带，那里的关键基础设施大多早已被摧毁。分析人士说，他们似乎正在盘算：自己能让沙特——世界最大石油出口国之一——承受的痛苦，要多于沙特能让他们承受的痛苦。
不久之后，年仅29岁的穆罕默德王储在其担任沙特国防部长的首批举措中，向胡塞武装宣战，誓言恢复也门政府——而那个时候，对方不过是一群乌合之众的叛军。
两周后，穆罕默德王储计划主办他那场旗舰级的年度投资峰会。届时，各国领导人、亿万富翁和企业高管本应齐聚利雅得，与沙特官员和基金经理们把酒寒暄。
沙特高级王室成员、前沙特情报机构负责人图尔基·费萨尔亲王表示，尽管沙特在外交政策上历来偏爱“克制”，但胡塞已经逾越了沙特领导层耐心的底线。他在上周接受沙特《阿拉伯新闻》采访时说：“克制，已不再可行。”
practice.critical_en: If a militia with almost nothing left to lose can hurt a wealthy state more than it gets hurt, what does that say about the limits of military power?
practice.critical_zh: 如果一支几乎没什么可失去的武装，能给一个富有的国家造成的伤害大于自己承受的伤害，那这是否说明军事力量本身就有极限？
practice.answer:
1. Yet the prince, Saudi Arabia’s de facto ruler, has few options as he confronts an asymmetrical conflict with an adversary that has become stronger since he led a disastrous war against it a decade ago, analysts say.

2. They have also hit at the heart of Prince Mohammed’s ambitions to transform Saudi Arabia from an insular, oil-dependent nation into a global hub for business and tourism.

3. The Houthis, who rule over bomb-scarred countryside where most critical infrastructure has already been destroyed, appear to be calculating that they can inflict more pain on Saudi Arabia, one of the world’s largest exporters of oil, than the kingdom can inflict on them, analysts say.

4. Soon after, Prince Mohammed, in one of his first acts as Saudi Arabia’s 29-year-old minister of defense, pledged to restore the Yemeni government by declaring war against the Houthis, at the time a ragtag group of rebels.

5. In two weeks, Prince Mohammed is planning to host his flagship annual investment summit, during which world leaders, billionaires and executives were expected to descend upon the city to hobnob with Saudi officials and fund managers.

6. Prince Turki Al Faisal, a senior Saudi royal and a former Saudi intelligence chief, said that while the kingdom had always preferred “restraint” in its foreign policy, the Houthis had exceeded the limits of the Saudi leadership’s patience. “Restraint is no longer operable,” he said in an interview last week with a Saudi newspaper, Arab News.
